News.title: Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ in broad daylight attack at country park – as cops hunt man in his 30s
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PARK HORROR Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ in broad daylight attack at country park – as cops hunt man in his 30s

A WOMAN was allegedly sexually assaulted at a park in a sickening broad daylight attack.

Cops said they have stepped up patrols in the area as detectives hunt a man described as white and aged in his 30s.

The sexual assault reportedly happened in a wooded area of Newstead and Annesley Country Park in Nottinghamshire.

The force said the incident occurred shortly after 11am on Tuesday (August 4).





Officers have launched a major investigation and increased their presence in the area.

Detective Inspector Ed Cook, of Nottinghamshire Police, has sought to reassure the community.

He said: “While incidents of this nature are extremely rare, they are obviously very concerning for the public.

“I would like to reassure people we have a large team of officers working on this investigation and we are doing everything we can to find the person responsible.



“The suspect has been described as a white man aged in his 30s.

“Public safety remains our top priority and extra patrols will continue to be carried out in the area.

“I’d also encourage the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious or concerning behaviour to us immediately.”

Police have urged anyone who saw anything suspicious around the time of the attack to come forward.



Officers are also appealing for anyone with information which could help identify the suspect to contact them.

Anyone with information is asked to call Nottinghamshire Police on 101, quoting incident number 38 of 7 August.

Information can also be passed anonymously to the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Terrifying moment huge hippo charges at boat full of tourists as beast lunges out of the water in pursuit
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a huge hippo charges at a boat packed with tourists before lunging through the water in a furious pursuit.

Viral footage captures the heart-stopping moment the massive male beast suddenly gives chase in Botswana, forcing the fleeing boat to speed away.



The tourists had been hoping for a glimpse of Africa’s spectacular wildlife when they spotted the lone hippo in the distance.

But their thrilling wildlife encounter quickly turned into a terrifying battle to escape the enormous beast.



The captain slowed the boat to avoid disturbing the territorial animal before issuing a chilling warning to his passengers.

Oznur Bell, the tourist who captured the moment on camera said: “After watching his behaviour for a moment, he calmly said, ‘Hold on-we need to speed up now before he decides to come after us.’



“The moment we accelerated, we looked back and realized the hippo was chasing us.”

The shocking footage shows the hulking animal powering through the water as it relentlessly pursues the boat.

For several terrifying moments, the tourists were left staring back at the furious beast as it bobbed in and out of the water behind them.

The videographer said: “For a few moments, every single person in the boat was genuinely worried.”



Oznur described the terrifying encounter as “one of the most terrifying moments I’ve ever experienced.”

According to the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, common hippos can grow to a staggering 16.5ft long and 5.2ft tall at the shoulder.

Adult males can weigh between 3,500 and almost 10,000lbs – making the colossal mammals roughly the weight of a mid-length SUV.

Despite their fearsome size and reputation, hippos are herbivores and do not view humans as prey.

Researchers at the University of Pretoria say hippos kill around 500 people across Africa every year – more than twice as many as lions.



The enormous animals are territorial and can aggressively defend their patches of water.

That means an unsuspecting boat entering their territory can quickly become a dangerous target.

The monstrous male eventually called off the chase, allowing the shaken tourists to escape.

But the dramatic encounter also showcased the astonishing way hippos move through shallow water.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rather than relying solely on traditional swimming strokes, the powerful animals can propel themselves by pushing off the bottom in a bizarre galloping or bounding motion.



The furious hippo put the remarkable technique on full display as it thundered through the water after the fleeing boat.

News.title: How Russian public is PAYING drone pilots to carry out sick ‘human safari’ attacks on innocent Ukrainian civilians
News.content:
TWISTED Russian civilians have been accused of paying for sick “human safari” hunting missions targeting defenceless Ukrainians on the streets.

Drone pilots working within the Russian army are “wilfully targeting civilians for monetary gain” under Vladimir Putin‘s evil rule, a former Nato analyst told The Sun.



Terrifying footage this week showed Yuriy, a 52-year-old grocer, running for his life as he was chased down by a Kremlin suicide drone.

The Ukrainian was left with serious shrapnel wounds as the UAV exploded as it struck the grocer’s tent where he was selling fruit and vegetables.



Harrowing footage was released just a few days later and captured another drone attack on a Ukrainian civilian in Sumy.

A Russian drone pursues a local appearing to toy with him before the operator makes the drone explode in a huge blast.



The horror scenes make up just a couple of the thousands of senseless attacks on civilians by Russia during the war in Ukraine with Kherson becoming known as the grim epicentre of the attacks.

Dr Patrick Bury, a warfare and counter-terrorism expert and former Nato analyst, says the brutality highlights how Putin has created a regime which is “completely rotten to the core”.



He told The Sun: “[Russia is] going in and they’re basically intentionally targeting civilians.

“It’s become known as the Kherson safari, essentially civilian hunting missions.

“It shows we’re at the real bottom of the barrel of human conduct in war.”

Dr Bury says the human safaris would be considered one of the worst atrocities committed by Moscow should they ever face consequences.

The term human safari is most well known due to the 1990s siege of Sarajevo.



Wealthy tourists were accused of making weekend trips to the besieged city and paying Serbian fighters to shoot civilians in the streets.

Dr Bury fears a similar pattern of abuse could be repeated in Ukraine after several worrying reports from independent journalists in Kyiv.

He claims: “It looks like a fusion between military units like the eighth Artillery Regiment and certain people in there who are drone operators.



“They have been accused of using crowdfunding from Russian civilians to gain money.

“They’re wilfully targeting civilians for monetary gain and propaganda gain.

“The fact that there’s been no one brought to task speaks volumes about the Russian military – the laws of war are clearly not a priority for them.”

In Kherson alone, Human Rights Watch (HRW) found at least 45 drone strikes carried out by Russian forces that appeared to deliberately target civilians.

Dozens of these cases were filmed and shared across Russian social media and Telegram channels.



In almost every example seen, HRW claims they believe the drone operator was purposely targeting a civilian or civilian infrastructure like a bus or parking lot.

Intentionally killing civilians during an armed conflict is a serious war crime, under international humanitarian law, such as the Geneva Conventions.

A United Nations probe during the conflict has found Russia guilty of committing crimes against humanity in the occupied regions of Ukraine.



The UN report states that large numbers of Ukrainian civilians have been targeted in a “widespread and systematic manner” at the hands of Russia.

Ukraine’s former deputy minister at the Ministry of Internal Affairs Anton Gerashchenko also condemned the human hunts.

He blasted: “Russian human safari is spreading. Russia‘s war crimes are mounting up.”

Back in April, three separate strikes on public spaces in the Nikopol district killed 10 and injured over 50 civilians within three days.

Russian FPVs hit two passenger buses, killing four civilians while a second in the nearby Chervonohryhorivka municipality wounded five.



A drone also struck a civilian car, killing one and injuring another as a day earlier five were killed when a Kremlin drone struck a civilian market in Nikopol.

Much like this year, the number of civilian attacks often surges in summer, Dr Bury says.

“Between summer 2025 and by October 2025, it was up to about 200 confirmed dead and over 2,000 wounded in these kinds of attacks.

“And they’re targeting everyone, they’re targeting shops, people going out for a cigarette, children in playgrounds even people on their way home from work.”

One of the scariest parts of these attacks is how defenceless the civilians are when the deadly UAVs lock onto their positions.



The drones can be operated by a soldier who watches a camera which allows them to track a target even if they try to run or hide.

“It’s not as if civilians in these areas are equipped with electromagnetic jammers so you can hear them and take cover and that is about it,” Dr Bury added.

For experts such as Patrick, the fact Russians allegedly partake in such heinous activities comes down to the example set by their despotic leader.

Dr Bury said: “There’s a lot of great things that have come out of Russia but ultimately it is quite a brutalised place, especially since the Soviets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And certainly in this war, you get to the front line and you’re put into a meat storm where you’re given a gun and then just told to charge the enemy to be quickly wiped down in a human wave attack.



“I think all this plays into a kind of normalisation of this kind of brutal behaviour.”

News.title: ‘Loving’ dad, 44, killed after being hit by six vehicles including cop car on major A-road is pictured as tributes paid
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC SMASH ‘Loving’ dad, 44, killed after being hit by six vehicles including cop car on major A-road is pictured as tributes paid

TRIBUTES have been paid for a “loving” dad who was killed in a six vehicle horror crash on a major A-road.

Gerard Trojanowski, 44, tragically died after being hit by multiple vehicles, including a marked police car, on the A40 in Wales.



Cops scrambled to the scene in Carmarthen at around 9.50pm on July 28 after reports of a pedestrian on the carriageway.

According to police, as they rushed to the busy road, five vehicles and one cop car hit the dad.



Gerard was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

His family said: “Gerard was a loving husband and father. A wonderful and generous person with a good heart.

“He will always be in our memories. As a family we ask for privacy during this difficult time.”

After the tragedy, which saw the busy road shut for a day, Dyfed-Powys Police made a mandatory referral to the Independent Office of Police Conduct.

Cops also issued a wider appeal for any information regarding the incident.

News.title: Putin unleashes deadly ballistic missile bombardment as child among three dead just hours after Ukraine stadium blitzed
News.content:
A CHILD is among at least three people who have been killed after Vladimir Putin unleashed another deadly missile barrage near Kyiv.

It came just hours after the dictator blitzed one of Ukraine‘s largest sports stadiums on the eve of a top-flight match.



Moscow has ramped up attacks on Kyiv in recent months, but has been on the receiving end of some long-range Ukrainian drone attacks.

Russian forces pummelled the Ukrainian capital on Tuesday night, launching 28 missiles in a 20-minute nightmare that became one of the deadliest onslaughts this year.



At least 21 people died and dozens of homes were blown up.

Early this morning, a quick-fire salvo of ballistic missiles struck just east of the city in the Brovary district.

A child and two adults were killed in the village of Pukhivka, while at least three others were wounded.

Houses and cars were damaged by falling debris and a non-residential building was set ablaze, according to Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration.



Shocking pictures from the heart of the action show firefighters tackling infernos cropping up across the city.

Witnesses reported hearing dozens of explosions and several air raid alerts amid the onslaught.

Ukraine’s state emergency service DSNS shared pictures of devastated buildings and garages, adding: “The number of victims is being clarified.”



Russia claimed to have blitzed a key factory that manufactures Ukrainian warheads.

Kyiv has been desperate to rebuild its stock of missile interceptors.

The Ukrainian Air Force was not able to destroy a single incoming Iskander-M ballistic missile overnight.

President Volodymyr Zelensky has meanwhile landed in the Serbian capital Belgrade to try to forge greater economic and security ties with President Aleksandar Vučić.

Despite the Ukrainian leader pushing to build wider support for Ukraine, Vučić has refused to apply sanctions to Russia.



Earlier this week, Zelensky mourned the “horrific casualties and destruction” caused by Putin’s last barrage.

He added that having stronger interceptor capability “could have saved lives”.

Ukraine’s supply of interceptors from allies has been “significantly reduced” this year, but Zelensky will be hopeful of getting a Patriot production license from the US.

Kyiv launched its own strikes overnight, hitting two oil depots deep inside Russia as well as Moscow-linked shadow ships in the Black Sea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zelensky has ruthlessly targeted Russian oil refineries this year, plunging the country into a fuel crisis.



Attempts to reach a peace deal have stalled of late, leading to an escalation in attacks.

News.title: The mystery of Mexico’s vast ‘Zone of Silence’ with no radio signal plagued by ‘alien’ sightings & mutated plants
News.content:
RADIO SILENCE The mystery of Mexico’s vast ‘Zone of Silence’ with no radio signal plagued by ‘alien’ sightings & mutated plants

SECONDS after a dazzling ball of light illuminates the sky above the vast expanse of desert, the object darts away at a “dizzying” speed and vanishes from view.

The extraordinary sight is just one of many reports of unexplained glowing objects in the sky in a remote corner of northern Mexico known as the Zone of Silence.



The 31-mile wide area deep in the Chihuahuan Desert has inspired many legends over the decades – drawing comparisons to the Bermuda Triangle and Area 51.

Phones stop working, radio signals fail and compasses spin out of control in this desolate part of the Mapimí Biosphere Reserve, according to those who have visited the area.



Many believe the phenomena are explained by a mystery electromagnetic phenomenon caused by the metals in the desert soil.

The area’s supernatural reputation first took off in 1970 when a US Air Force rocket went wildly off target and crash-landed in the desert.



At the time, some believed it was due to the area’s magnetic anomalies.

The area is known to be a hotspot for celestial activity, with meteorites reported to frequently come crashing down to earth in the desert.



But some claim the Zone of Silence attracts more than just asteroids, with numerous reports of UFO and extraterrestrial sightings.

Benjamín Marcelo Palacios Perches has lived his entire life on the edge of the zone and was born in nearby Escalón, Chihuahua.

He owns a ranch that he has named “Zona del Silencio” after the famous landmark, and offers accommodation, traditional sweatlodge ceremonies, stargazing and tours into the zone for visitors.

The 71-year-old frequently visits the zone and has had many mystifying experiences that he believes have no earthly explanation.

He told The Sun: “I and many other visitors have observed disc-shaped objects, triangular objects, cylindrical craft, and also balls of light and fireballs that make erratic movements.



“Movements that no human-made craft could perform, let alone dart away at the dizzying speeds we have witnessed.

“I have had the opportunity to observe all those objects, lights and fireballs.”



Benjamin said he experienced first-hand the electromagnetic anomalies associated with the zone that mean compasses and phones don’t work.

He believes the area acts as a “powerful magnet attracting celestial bodies”.

“I am absolutely convinced that these strange electromagnetic powers exist in the Zone of Silence – I have experienced them myself, but I am not the only one,” he said.

“When I was very young, I used to hear my grandfather and his generation speak of these strange occurrences.



“Now, I hear newer and newer generations – successive waves of people -continuing to speak of the same phenomena.”

The Zone of Silence is widely reported to have first been coined in 1966 when Augusto Harry de la Peña, the leader of an expedition for oil company Pemex, experienced problems with his radio.

Since then, thousands have visited the zone and come up with their own theories – which sceptics have dismissed as inventions to attract tourists.

Some of the claims include sightings of mutant animals and plants.

Among the more fantastical stories swirling around the zone are tales of encounters with tall, fair-haired beings who speak perfect Spanish and ask for water before they disappear without a trace.



Experts say the real reason for the stunted signals in the area is actually due to subterranean deposits of magnetite messing with receptors.

The extremely remote and mountainous region is also responsible for the poor reception much like many isolated areas and deserts.

Signal can actually be found in the Zone of Silence but only in certain areas.



The supernatural claims have also been widely debunked as urban legends passed down through generations.

Dr Fernando Ortega Gutierrez, a researcher at the Institute of Geology in Mexico City, said he had visited the zone and believed the electromagnetic phenomena could be explained by the soil’s composition.

“Our compass did not work, giving chaotic orientations of the needle,” he said.

“On examining the ground we were working at, we explained that fact, blaming itono the abundance of detrital grains of magnetite in the soils.

“The mountains around the area may be rich in magnetite-rich granites or iron ores.”



Travellers continue to come from around the world to witness these strange phenomena, including US digital nomad Hannah Pinkerton, who lives in Mexico teaching Spanish.

She visited the Zone of Silence last year and camped the night in the desert with a tour group, in an experience she documented on her travel website Destined for Adventure.

“It’s really beautiful, the sunset was really beautiful, and it was a nice camping experience – there is not a lot out there,” she said.

“It’s very quiet and peaceful, there’s not a lot of trees, there’s not a lot of mountains, there’s just a lot of sand and open land.”

Hannah said the Zone of Silence is not well known outside the Spanish-speaking world, but it is very well known in Mexico with friends telling her before she left that she might “see a spaceship”.



She said she is “open minded and curious” about the paranormal but did not see anything out of the ordinary.

“It’s a vast desert and it’s very quiet and peaceful, the radios and cell phones and things don’t work, so there is not a lot of distraction to take you away from the quietness,” she said.

Benjamin agreed the remoteness and beauty of the zone – as well as its strange phenomena – is what has “captivated” him for decades.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It is a remarkable place; one feels a very special energy that recharges the body, making one feel dynamic and highly active – as if infused with a surge of energy,” he said.

“That is the sensation one experiences in the Zone of Silence.”

News.title: Horrifying moment fast food staff scramble for cover as mass shooter fires into store window during deadly rampage
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment desperate workers clamber over each other after a gunman shoots into a drive-thru window amid a sick murder spree.

Terrifying footage captures the moment In-n-Out workers scramble for cover in the Idaho mass shooting which left three dead on August 1.



Shocking CCTV from inside the restaurant shows at least nine employees chaotically falling over each other as they try to evacuate the area.

The gunman, 24-year-old Chad Williams, acted alone before dying of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, officials said.



His motive remains unclear.

Now harrowing video, released by the Twin Falls Police Department, shows the moment the carnage began when Williams opened fire at the drive-thru window.

read more world news GUN HORROR At least three dead after 'gunman opens fire' outside burger restaurant

Employee Ashley Garibay, 23, was the first to be shot and later died from her injuries.

Williams then fatally shoots his second victim, 59-year-old Christopher Claunch, who was inside another car.



At that moment, former Twin Falls and Idaho State Police Officer Austin “AJ” Scott who happened to be there at the time starts running toward the gunman.

Williams takes aim and strikes the ex-cop.

Scott’s father later wrote on Facebook that his son was “critically injured” as a result and is facing a “long road of surgeries, rehab and recovery”.



After calmly parking his car, Williams then peers back into the restaurant’s payment window and fires another shot at employees who were inside rendering aid to Garibay.

His handgun jams and he walks back to his car to retrieve a rifle, offering staff a moment to escape

At this moment another hero off-duty cop jumps the counter inside the restaurant and can be seen instructing the workers to run for cover as he aims his gun at the window and later the door.

Now armed with a rifle, Williams fires at people in their cars at the drive-thru before he returns to the payment window to be met with the unidentified trooper.

They both exchange fire.



Williams then retreats from the window momentarily before returning and firing another shot inside.

He strikes a “Good Samaritan” who is attempting to assist the off-duty trooper and render aid to the victim inside, according to the video.

Williams then shoots at multiple vehicles stopped at a nearby red light, striking three victims, before running to a nearby Tesla charging station.

He fires at the first Tesla he sees before fatally shooting Dale Schultz, 66, and hitting the man’s now gravely injured wife, Reinette, inside their car – all while a third armed good Samaritan is firing at him.

Still holding his gun he then moved inside the nearby Twin Falls Visitor’s Center with the video showing two people cowering in the corner as he sulks around the location.



Finally then makes his way to a hiking trail, where a brave bystander tried to halt him to give others time to run away.

In a climactic moment, a officer’s bodycam footage captures the moment he spots Williams on a nearby river bank.

He shouts: “Hey, show me your hands.”

At that very moment, Williams “dies of a self-inflicted gunshot wound and falls into the canyon.”

A statement at the end of the video said: “The Twin Falls Police Department is certain that additional acts of heroism and rendering aid to those in need contributed to the saving of lives,” the statement reads.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“At least ten people were left injured from the mass shooting, which remains under investigation, according to the department.”

In a statement, the fast food chain said: “In-n-Out is heartbroken as we mourn the tragic loss of three innocent lives, one of them being our Associate Ashley Garibay.”

News.title: Bristol Airport live: Families stranded as passengers rage 'let us out' after mass flight chaos
News.content:
UK family share nightmare trying to get home from holiday

Welsh mum Charmaine Hines has told of her nightmare trying to get home with her young family from a summer holiday in Barcelona.

She, her husband, and their three kids - aged four, 10 and 12 - have been stuck in Barcelona Airport, caught up in Friday's sudden Bristol Airport closure.

Charmaine and her family were supposed to fly at 10:05pm last night with easyJet and, well, that has not happened.

Last night they spent three and a half hours at Barcelona Airport with no access to food as they waited "as we had to go and collect our hold luggage", the mum-of-three told the Bristol Live.

Thankfully, easyJet did offer them hotel at 10.30pm, meaning the family did not have to spend the night on the airport floor.

But, communication has still been poor - we've "checked the app and [our] rearranged flight is already two hours delayed".

"No email or text from easyJet," the mum said, adding the only way the family have received any updates is by proactively checking the airline's app.

Charmaine slammed easyJet's handling of the situation and their lack of communication.

She said of last night that the "easyJet advisor at Barcelona airport was no help and didn’t have a clue what to say or do.

"No care from easyJet the fact we’ve not eaten for nearly 24 hours. They expect us to have unlimited money to pay for everything, [meanwhile] we collect receipts and then will have to await refunds!"

She added: "It is not ideal with [it being] summer holidays, and having to wait - and no idea how long for - for our money back!"

Mum Charmaine could not believe her eyes to see no easyJet staff available to help as the Bristol Airport outage continues (Image: Charmaine Hines)

To add insult to injury, the Welsh mum revealed that the family have rocked up to Barcelona Airport this morning to find no easyJet support staff present to assist with any queries.

News.title: Donald Trump's wild week saw him melt down over his ballroom and chase a toddler around
News.content:
Donald Trump's wild week saw him melt down over his ballroom and chase a toddler around

Trump found himself chasing a toddler around a stage in Las Vegas, which was more entertaining than anything ever put on at the Sphere. Here's your weekly roundup of the nonsense coming out of Trumpworld

Donald Trump should have worked out now that he can't win them all. He's spent half the week fuming at various people - his Defence Secretary, the DC circuit court, Jeannine Pirro. And he spent more time than you'd expect chasing toddlers around in Vegas, but we'll come to that. Yes, Trump suffered various setbacks this week - but it looks like he's going to win at least one thing - the confirmation of Todd Blanche, his former personal lawyer as Attorney General.

‌



Let's take a look at how this week has unfolded in Trumpworld

‌



Trump fumes over ballroom blockage

View 3 Images Well, this could be problematic (Image: AP Photo/Jose Luis Magana)

‌



We talk about Trump having meltdowns a lot around here. But the one he suffered when the DC appeals court ruled 2-1 that no, he didn't have the right to demolish bits of the White House without congressional approval.

"We are aware of no instance in American history in which a President, unilaterally and using privately collected funds, demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now," judges Patricia Millett and Bradley Garcia wrote in their opinion.

It's part of a long running court battle where critics of his plan to build a dictator bunker and massive ballroom on the site of what used to be the East Wing, Trump had demolished without asking.

‌



The court of appeals upheld the injunction, but gave a two week stay to allow Trump to take it to the Supreme Court.

And in a FOUR HUNDRED AND EIGHTY SEVEN WORD POST on Truth Social, Trump said he was going to do just that.

He argued in the post that the judgement was illegal, because he, like, really really wants to build a ballroom and dictator bunker.

‌



He wrote: "The Military and Secret Service are viewing this horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful ruling as a National Security threat to our Nation in that the entire Complex is being built for the protection of our Country and, additionally, all future Presidents."

He went on to moan: "The Circuit Court also refused to acknowledge that the desperately needed, and totally secure Ballroom, which is being built ahead of schedule and under budget, is a Gift from President Trump and Great Patriots of the United States of America. The entire Complex, Military and all, is largely built, fabricated, and paid for. Much is already on site, or being delivered. Why didn't they bring this case long prior to construction starting?"

Now, I can answer that one. They didn't bring the case before construction started, because you repeatedly lied about what you were doing, and nobody knew what you were actually planning to build until construction had started.

‌



It's going to be an interesting case for the Surpemes. The law is pretty clear that he didn't have the right to do what he did. And allowing a President free rein to demolish whatever national landmark he wants to because he needs a subterranean palace to hide out in when it all goes south....a ballroom, sorry, he needs a ballroom...is a pretty terrible precedent to set.

But, on the other hand...what are they going to do, order him to put the East Wing back up?

He ripped up the new helipad

View 3 Images It had only just been laid (Image: AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

‌



In another unnecessary and costly renovation which Trump is not handling at all well, the President ordered an estimated $5-6m worth of work that had been done on the new helipad on the South Lawn be torn up because he didn't like the angle.

Trump ordered a massive round helipad, featuring a massive Seal of the President, be installed because apparently the new Marine One choppers have been damaging the grass.

A great deal of work had been done on this already when this week, Trump took a look at it and decided he didn't like the natural slope of the lawn. He apparently wanted the helipad to line up with the horizon, so workers ripped up the work they'd done and got to work levelling the South Lawn off. Trump insists chopper manufacturer Sikorsky is paying for the work in full, but he says a lot of things.

‌



Pirro survives for now

View 3 Images Watch this space (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Despite being one of the least effective prosecutors in the United States, former Fox News blowhard Jeannine Pirro is still apparently a US Attorney. For now.

Trump and Pirro are on the rocks after she dropped the charges against the Olympic canoeist who Trump claims "vandalised" the Lincoln reflecting pool. Late last week the Justice Department and the Department of the Interior came out and admitted the damage to the pool's surface wasn't actually vandalism, it was just Trump's handpicked contractors doing a shoddy job.

‌



Pirro remains unfired for now, but Trump remains convinced sick vandals took a box cutter to his lovely pool.

Two Brits go to Washington

Early this week, Ed Miliband flew to DC for a 90 minute "warm and productive" meeting with Marco Rubio. They discussed the special relationship, NATO and Ukraine - as well as, of course, the Strait of Hormuz. Rubio's team put out a slightly sniffier readout of the meeting, noting there had been a discussion of Europe paying for its own security.

But the most fun happened just before the meeting, when reporters loudly asked Miliband if he still thought Donald Trump was an idiot and a racist. Miliband neither confirmed nor denied.

‌



A few days later, another familiar face showed up in a photo with a member of the Trump administration. Reform UK's Robert Jenrick is, for some reason, in Washington and met with JD Vance. It's the second time they've met in the last 12 months. Almost exactly this time last year, Vance visited the UK, and Jenrick - then still a Tory - managed to get an audience for him and Chris Philp. It is entirely unclear what brings Jenrick, whose job is - and I had to look this up - Treasury spokesman, is doing in Washington the week before a crucial by-election...

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Trump is running out of bombs

Trump and "secretary of war" Pete Hegseth reportedly had a barney while they were at Camp David for a cabinet meeting last week.

‌



The topic of the row is something that people have been reporting for quite a while - and that apparently everyone was kind of aware of except Trump. America's munitions stockpiles are running out.

According to The Washington Post, Trump demanded answers from Hegseth about why he'd been misled on the shortages, which threaten to limit his ability to expand the offensive in Iran, should he decide to bomb even more things.

Pete, naturally, blamed his deputy, Stephen Feinberg, for the shortages and for Trump not being kept up to date.

‌



After this blowup was reported by The Washington Post, the White House nonsense machine kicked in. Karoline Leavitt herself declared that the falling-out "never happened".

In previous administrations, the outright denial of a story would probably be enough to kill a story, or at least make the public think it might not be true. It tells you a lot about how casually this administration lies to the American people that this has not happened.

Anyway, Trump kind of confirmed it was true in a late-night rage post on Truth Social, where he insisted America still had loads of bombs left...but had a pop at the "leakers" who told The Washington Post what had gone on.

‌



Cassidy caves

And now we get to Trump getting exactly what he wants.

Republican Senator Bill Cassidy said Friday he’ll back Donald Trump's former personal lawyer, Todd Blanche’s nomination as attorney general, likely paving the way for Blanche to be confirmed to lead President Trump’s Justice Department.

The Louisiana senator announced his support on the Senate floor after Blanche’s confirmation was thrown into doubt over opposition from two other Republican senators, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Susan Collins of Maine.

‌



Blanche’s path to confirmation has been complicated over a settlement of Trump’s lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service that’s drawn intense scrutiny by Republicans and Democrats alike.

The settlement called for the creation of a $1.8 billion slush fund to compensate people who feel mistreated by the criminal justice system - largely aimed at January 6th rioters - and provided Trump and family members with immunity from tax audits.

"Mr. Blanche is not perfect," Cassidy said, before arguing essentially that Blanche is likely better than anyone else Trump could nominate.

Article continues below

Trump chased a toddler around a stage in Vegas

Not much more I can add to this one, except to say that it was at least as entertaining at anything that's ever been put on at the Sphere.

News.title: Another hosepipe ban starts today - what is exempt and what you can't do in your gardens
News.content:
Another hosepipe ban starts today - what is exempt and what you can't do in your gardens

Another water company has imposed a hosepipe ban on millions of customers as low rainfall and another incoming heatwave puts pressure on water supplies

View 3 Images New hosepipe restrictions are coming into force (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

A new hosepipe ban has started for nearly 2 million people today as the UK braces for a fifth heatwave.

‌



Most of south-west England will be hit following a prolonged period of dry weather, as South West Water announced the restriction. All customers in Devon, Cornwall, parts of Dorset and Somerset and the Isles of Scilly will be subject to the temporary conditions, which started from 1am today.

‌



The water company said a dry summer, significantly below average rainfall and high demand had increased pressure on the local water resources and led to the temporary ban.

‌



Met Office issues heatwave verdict and names two regions facing 36C on Thursday READ MORE :

View 3 Images Aerial view of dry fields at the Falmouth Golf Club, in Cornwall, on July 31 (Image: Getty Images)

What will people not be allowed to do?

Restrictions have been placed on non-essential activities like filling swimming pools or paddling pools, watering gardens, washing cars, boats, patios and windows.

People will still be allowed to use water for washing, cooking, drinking and flushing toilets. Customers can also carry out activities without a hosepipe - like using a watering can on flowers and plants.

‌



What are the exemptions?

The hosepipe ban does not apply to certain customers, which includes:

Blue Badge holders

People on the water company's Priority Services Register and unable to make reasonable adjustments due to a health condition or disability

Cases where human health and safety need to be protected

Water is needed for animal welfare, including pets, livestock and fish

There is also an exception for people who are not using water from the mains supply, for examples if it has been taken from a recycled water storage system.

‌



View 3 Images Dried land at Glastonbury, Somerset, on July 31 (Image: Getty Images)

Why has the new ban come into force?

South West Water said a dry summer, significantly below average rainfall and high demand had increased pressure on the local water resources and led to the temporary ban.

The water company added that rainfall in the region has been considerably below the seasonal average for several months. South West Water said this temporary restriction will "ensure a resilient supply of water to its customers".

‌



Last month was the driest July for England and Wales since records began in 1836, according to provisional figures released by the Met Office.

What else have customers been asked to do?

South West Water has asked people in the impacted region to take shorter showers and turn off the tap while brushing their teeth. Customers can also rub washing machines and dishwashers only with full loads.

Sam Bottomley, South West Water, said: "Our teams have been working tirelessly to protect supplies for customers. We've maximised water production wherever possible, increased leak detection and repairs, moved water around our network and introduced a wide range of operational measures to make the best use of the water available."

Article continues below

Bottomley added: "Every litre saved now will help protect our rivers and water resources while drought conditions continue. By making small changes to how we use water, our customers can make a real difference."

Which other water companies have restrictions in place?

Some companies have had bans in place since mid-July. Nine water companies have temporary bans in place: Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Essex and Suffolk Water, Southern Water, South East Water, South West Water, Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water and Thames Water.

This comes as new heat alerts are to come into force as the UK braces for its fifth heatwave of the year, bringing scorching highs of 36C. The Met Office said temperatures will climb through the weekend, with a high of 36C expected in parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday.

News.title: Frances Barber fulfils 40-year dream to land heartbreaking Corrie role
News.content:
She’s worked with everyone from Dustin Hoffman to Christian Slater, but it was Corrie’s Rita who“gobsmacked” RSC actress Frances Barber into starstruck silence. Joining Coronation Street later this month as Celeste - the ebullient estranged aunt of Bernie Winter-Alahan (Jane Hazlegrove) - will be the highlight of her career.

She says: “The truth is that I’ve wanted to walk the cobbles for 40 years. It was on my bucket list. I’m a complete and utter fanatic. I grew up on it. I’m from a council estate in Wolverhampton, one of six kids. I know Wolverhampton isn’t Weatherfield, but it’s not that dissimilar.

“I used to be a Saturday girl in Marks & Spencer and the shoppers were like all the women on Corrie – strong, blunt, down-to-earth and very funny. I’ve loved them and respected them all my life, so it was always a dream. I thought ‘one day I will walk the cobbles.’ And I did, so I’m over the moon about it. It’s absolutely one of my career highlights.”

During her 47-year-career, Frances, 68, has worked with the prestigious Royal Shakespeare Company and performed at the National Theatre. But when she encountered Barbara Knox, who plays Rita Tanner, on the Corrie set, she says: “I was very, very nervous.

‌



View 7 Images Frances Barber's personal picture from filming on Corrie in character as Celeste: Gareth Pierce, Amy Robbins, Antony Cotton, Aaron McCusker, Jodie Prenger

“I passed Barbara Knox and my heart skipped a beat. I was literally gobsmacked. I didn’t speak to her, I don’t think anything would have come out of my mouth actually, because I grew up watching her. I didn’t get to see Bill Roache [Ken Barlow], but I’ve taken pictures of all their dressing rooms. And I’ve got a picture of me pretending to pull a pint in the Rovers Return that I’ve sent to everybody I know.

“I’ve driven all of my friends mad – ‘here’s a picture of me outside the Rovers, here’s a picture of me outside Roy’s Rolls.’ They all went, ‘enough!’ But you can’t imagine how excited I was, I really am a fan girl!”

Celeste arrives on the cobbles on August 19, looking for her niece, Bernie. Discovering she’s away, she visits the undertakers and starts organising a Dolly Parton-themed funeral for a ‘friend’. Eventually, she tells Todd Grimshaw (Gareth Pierce) that the funeral is actually her own, as she has cancer and has only six weeks to live.

‌



View 7 Images Francis Barber as Polonius and Ian McKellen as Hamlet in a production of William Shakespeare's Hamlet directed by Sean Mathias at The Theatre Royal Windsor (Image: Corbis via Getty Images)

Frances says: “She reminds me completely of the women that I adored and grew up with, such as Elsie Tanner. She’s straightforward, witty and clever and says it as it is. She’s a Dolly Parton fan, so she’s dressed head to foot in cow print and cowboy outfits. She even sings a bit of Dolly Parton at one point. She’s wonderful. It was the gift of a part for any actress my age and I relished it.”

But there’s no hero’s welcome from Bernie, because of a family fall-out involving Celeste and her twin-sister – Bernie’s mum. Luckily, the Corrie cast was the opposite.

She says: “The cast were so warm. When you’re a visiting artist, you’re in a hotel on your own, but they took me out to Pizza Express – Tony Maudsley (George Shuttleworth) Jane Hazlegrove, Amy Robbins (Christina) and Gareth. They really couldn’t have been nicer to me. It was lovely.”

‌



View 7 Images Sir Ian McKellen, Frances Barber and Patrick Stewart, pictured in 2009 (Image: Getty Images)

Starting out in theatre, aged 26, Frances joined the Royal Shakespeare Company - receiving Olivier award nominations for her stage roles in Camille and Uncle Vanya.

Her film career has included Mike Leigh’s Home Sweet Home with Timothy Spall and 1987’s Prick Up Your Ears with Gary Oldman and Julie Walters. Meanwhile, her TV credits include Whitstable Pearl, Doctor Who, Benidorm, Friday Night Dinner and Cold Feet.

Other career highlights include filming in Italy with Dustin Hoffman for the Netflix series Medici and appearing in London’s West End in One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest with Christian Slater.

‌



She says: “Dustin and Christian are two of the humblest, most professional people you could ever work with. Dustin kept saying, ‘was I ok? Was that ok?’ I was like ‘you’re asking me?’ But they don’t take their stardom seriously.”

View 7 Images Frances as The Bolter in Love in A Cold Climate (Image: BBC)

Enjoying a phenomenal career, Frances admits there have been lows as well as highs. Camille went to America, but they gave her role to Hollywood icon Kathleen Turner. She says: “I was really heartbroken about that, but that’s showbiz.”

Ten years ago, she was offered a job in America and moved to Hollywood, where she shed two stone after feeling under pressure to lose weight to get parts. She says: “I’m glad I went and got it out of my system and I’m very glad I went when I was older.

‌



“I think it’s very tricky for young actresses. I felt that pressure, even at my age and I lost loads of weight – I’ve put it all back on again unfortunately! Everyone goes to the gym all the time, so I was going to the gym, to Pilates, I was swimming. When I got back home everybody went ‘oh my God, you’ve disappeared!’”

View 7 Images Frances Barber as Nurse Ratched, Christian Slater as Randle P McMurphy in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (Image: Nils Jorgensen/Shutterstock)

It was a visit from her good friend Sir Ian McKellen that made her realise it was time to return to Britain. She says: “He came over because he had a film out and I went to the premiere with him. He said ‘you’ve done it, you haven’t failed, you’ve worked and now it’s time to come home because we all miss you.’ I burst into tears. I was homesick.”

Firm friends since the 1980s, Ian came to her rescue after a catastrophic accident in 2007, when Frances was knocked off her bike into the path of an oncoming lorry. She says: “We were doing King Lear in Stratford and we were about to embark on a world tour. I bought a bike – the worst idea I’ve ever had – and one day, going to rehearsals, I had this terrible accident.

‌



“I fell and I saw the whites of the eyes of the driver. I’m lucky to be alive. I broke my cruciate ligament and needed an operation and I just couldn’t walk. I was in a wheelchair and Ian took me in. He helped me get up and down the stairs and into and out of the bath – he was great.”

View 7 Images Corrie: Glenda Shuttelworth [JODIE PRENGER] spots a woman, Celeste [FRANCES BARBER], knocking on the door of No.7....

Six years later, Frances was in the wars again, this time after falling off a horse filming the Sky sitcom The Spa. “I had to dismount and I fell and landed on my knee. I ended up in a wheelchair again.”

Frances, who has had long-term relationships with director Danny Boyle and actor Neil Pearson, lives in Clerkenwell, central London, and is in a relationship again. She says: “He kind of lives with me, that’s all I’ll say. He’s not in the same business.”

‌



Once she finishes in Weatherfield, Frances is off to Belgium to begin filming the new series of the crime drama Bookish. But she’s been sharing her Corrie tales with Sir Ian, who had a stint on the cobbles in 2005, playing conman author Mel Hutchwright.

Frances says: “He’s in New Zealand doing Gandalf again. He’s very excited I’ve got this job and he’s made me promise that I’ll tell him when it’s on, so he can stream it in Wellington; he loves Corrie as much as me.”

*Frances makes her Coronation Street debut on August 19. Coronation Street airs weekdays on ITV at 8:30 PM and ITVX at 7 AM

News.title: Brian Reade: 'Farage said Brexit would stop the boats - we must ignore his cynical fantasies'
News.content:
When I was growing up I often heard sarcastic claims that ­winning the Second World War was the worst thing that had happened to Britain. Relatives who had survived the Blitz or fought abroad would ponder the point of their generation’s sacrifice when the German and Japanese ­economies were booming and ours was bust. Today I see a different downside to that vital victory over Nazism.

It has locked a huge group of Britons into a mental straitjacket, unable to let go of a war that has been eulogised out of all proportion. The blind fools, nearly all of whom were not alive in the early-1940s, are manipulated by right-wing ­opportunists who profit from viewing every event through the prism of Dunkirk or D-Day.

This week Nigel Farage tried to shake off questions about his dubious finances and his war of ideas with a bin when he announced he would stop the boats by marshalling the Royal Navy to drag them all back to France through “Operation Fortress”, which would be “the largest military operation in the English Channel since World War Two”. Despite the fact that we don’t possess a fully-functioning Navy (even the warship on the front of Reform’s Operation brochure was flogged to Brazil eight years ago) and military experts and French authorities all mocked his stunt as a ludicrous non-starter, Farage went up in the opinion polls. Because so many naive Brits swallow his cynical fantasy that the only way this country will be great is by turning the clock back 80-odd years.

‌



When France described Farage’s plan as a violation of its sovereignty, Reform MP Sarah Pochin tweeted: “Pity the French did not show the same resolve in defending their sovereignty in June 1940.” Which is lamentable in every sense of the word, especially in its ignorance. As many as 570,000 French people died in the Second World War, more than half of them civilians. The total of Britons killed was 450,000.

For years the Right has profited from peddling the insulting myth that British sacrifice alone defeated Hitler, therefore, we are superior to the rest of Europe. That lie won Brexit. Remember Vote Leave buses blaring the soundtrack to The Great Escape, billboards urging drivers to “Halt ze German advance! Vote Leave,” and Tory Mark Francois claiming: “My father was a D-Day veteran. He never submitted to bullying by any German. Neither will his son.” All tragic garbage.

But back to “Operation Fortress”. How come we need it when last summer Farage assured us that Reform’s mass deportations would end the small boats crisis? Wasn’t Brexit supposed to make Britain a border-secure fortress? Surely with Labour cutting Channel crossings by 44% this year, do we really need to distract what’s left of our Navy from monitoring ­Britain’s real enemies?

When you operate in Forties Fantasy World you don’t need to answer such questions. You just grab your dog whistle, claim the root of everyone’s problem is immigration, spout Churchillian rhetoric and tell the mugs that if you elect Reform, Britons never, ever, ever will be slaves. Which bumps up your popularity and reinforces the illusion that Britain can be magicked back to some glorious, all-white, problem-free past if we just put our trust in a dodgy salesman in a Union Jack suit with a boot full of snake oil. Snake oil sold in Spitfire-shaped bottles with instructions to be slugged back like a large glass of Vera Lynn.

‌

News.title: 'I won £2.7m on lottery but returned to stacking shelves at M&S – money never changed me'
News.content:
'I won £2.7m on lottery but returned to stacking shelves at M&S – money never changed me'

It has been just over 30 years since Elaine Thompson won £2.7million on the lottery with her husband Derek but she has explained why she kept working in M&S up until her recent retirement

View 4 Images Elaine and Derek Thompson landed the jackpot in 1995 (Image: PA)

Winning millions on the lottery has led to many examples of people getting too big for their boots — but this is not always the case.

‌



We recently reported how delivery driver Gary MacDonald won £5.2m on the lottery before kindly returning to his former workplace to hand out presents.

‌



Gary, 61, who has since retired, delivered parcels to shops across Lakeside Shopping Centre in Thurrock, Essex, where he worked for more than three decades before his life-changing win.

‌



Speaking about going back to enjoy the moment with his colleagues, he said: “I'm delighted to come out of retirement for the day to fulfil the promise I made myself.

“It's been great surprising my old colleagues, their faces have been a picture. I think we've done a brilliant job of surprising them and spreading the joy with today's deliveries.”

View 4 Images Elaine recently spoke with Timothy Schultz who knows how it feels to win the lottery (Image: YouTube/ Timothy Schultz)

‌



And while Gary proved that the money didn’t go to his head, one mum from Newcastle went a step further after her own lottery win. Elaine Thompson took on night shifts in Marks & Spencer, a job she enjoyed up until her recent retirement.

She last spoke publicly during a chat with Powerball winner Timothy Schultz who suffered an unexpected dark side after his 40p ticket landed him £23m.

Elaine meanwhile said she suffered no negativity from the windfall and that it gave her and her family the most incredible life.

‌



Her and husband Derek won £2.7million in December 1995 and they remain completely in love having been together for almost 50 years since they were teenagers.

But as for why Elaine, who is from Newcastle, went on to get up at 2am for night shifts in M&S all the way up until recently, she told Timothy on his YouTube channel: “I love to work. I can’t be in the house 10 hours, 12 hours a day.

View 4 Images Derek (left) and Elaine Thompson celebrating their National Lottery win with Elaine's brother Ian Allen who they gave £1m to (Image: PA)

‌



“It drives me insane. I mean, I’m nearly 70 now, so I had to retire. There has to be a time when you’ve got to stop. But I still miss work. And I worked for 50 years. I’d go back if I could.”

Timothy then questioned whether the lottery win changed her because he had noticed in some other winners that it magnified their personalities and led to extreme decision making.

However, Elaine simply said: “It hasn’t changed me at all. I’ll not change for anybody. So no, I wouldn’t change for anything.”

‌



And as for the greatest thing about winning the lottery with her husband, she said: “The major thing is my children have gone through university. They’re all on the housing, they’ve all got houses. They’re increasing them every time. They are happy, they’ve got children, I’ve got grandchildren.

“It’s just, we’ve had an extraordinary life. The things that I have done are extraordinary.

View 4 Images They also invested in racehorsing which is a shared passion (Image: Anthony Devlin / SWNS)

‌



“I mean, who would have thought a little girl from Wallsend, it’s a very small place, walking through the doors of Number 10? Never in a million years I would have dreamed I’d do that.”

Elaine has achieved a lot since the lottery win including turning a two-star rundown B&B in Lyme Regis, Dorset, into a five-star one within six months of buying it.

She also bought a restaurant after running the B&B for six years and this was another success.

‌



Derek and Elaine eventually moved back to the north east which is where she got a job she loved stacking shelves in M&S.

And as for how she has always lived her life, she concluded: “My philosophy is you go to bed with a smile, you get up with a smile, whatever happens through the day happens, you can’t, you can’t change that.”

Finally, for anyone fortunate enough to ever win the lottery, she offered the following advice: “If you do win, the decisions you make on the day are completely different to weeks down the line.

Article continues below

“So we always say, take at least a month before you make any decisions on what you’re going to do, where you’re gonna go, whatever.”

News.title: Woman loses 11 stone without leaving her home by using a wall to work out
News.content:
Woman loses 11 stone without leaving her home by using a wall to work out

Laci Gilbert dropped 159lbs with the help of the Simple lifestyle app and at-home Pilates

View 3 Images Laci Gilbert before and after losing weight (Image: Simple)

A woman has lost around 11 stone without leaving her home - and it's thanks to a lifestyle app called Simple. It helped her change her diet while incorporating wall Pilates routines from the comfort of her own home, and she says it's 'great for a busy person'.

Laci Gilbert, a mum who started her weight loss journey in 2023, weighed 275lbs before dropping to 116lbs - and she did this with the help of the Simple app and by doing home wall Pilates workouts. She has lost around 11 stone and says 'all you need is yourself'.

Laci said: "As working mums, wives, mothers, just family members, life takes over and sometimes we don't have time in the evenings to get ourselves to the gym or sometimes we just don't feel like moving. The Simple app gives you a no-excuse reason to get up and move, especially when you can do it at home with no equipment."



Simple is a clinically proven weight loss tool that has helped users lose over 18 million pounds. To use it, people just need to take a quiz and Simple builds a personalised plan, with handy features including food logging through typing, voice or photo; an intermittent fasting tracker; a NutriScanner, which is designed to help users understand the nutrition in meals; and daily workout plans.

What's more, users can currently save 80% off the app's weight loss plans using the code REACH. Then, once subscribed, there's a two-for-one deal where users can share their Simple premium with someone of their choice - for no added cost.

The Simple app can be downloaded 80% off Simple Buy Now on Simple Product Description Simple Life is a clinically proven weight loss tool that has helped users lose over 18 million pounds

She added: "It is great for a busy person who needs something to do at home or somebody who cannot afford a gym membership, equipment. All you need is yourself and a wall and you've got it."

One of the standout features with Simple is the in-app coach, Avo. Powered by AI, Avo is a personal wellness assistant which can answer questions right away, meaning users have 24/7 access to wellbeing and fitness advice whenever it's needed.

There's also an emotional support feature called Blinky for additional help. Blinky is described as a furry friend who cheers when users log meals, sulks when they don't, and spirals when ignored.

Another said: "I love, love this app. I've lost over 7lbs in two weeks. It's geared toward motivation and encouraging good health habits and behaviour. The calorie counter could be better, but at the end of the day, it's about losing weight. And it has got me there."
