News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree shock loan deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to relieve Andoni Iraola’s pre-season injury crisis
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL are set to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo to ease their defensive injury woes.

The shock move for the Uruguayan will start as a season-long loan, but Liverpool will have the option to make it permanent next summer.



Fabrizio Romano claims that Barca have green-lighted the switch, which will be signed off by all parties in the next 24 hours.

Araujo, 27, has made more than 200 appearances for the Catalan giants and helped them win LaLiga in three of the past four seasons.



He also finished last campaign as the most senior member of the club’s captaincy group following the departure of Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

So his signing will go down as a major coup for new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, who has been left light at the back by injuries.



Jeremy Jacquet is still recovering from a shoulder problem, Giovanni Leoni is not yet back after an ACL tear, while Joe Gomez has suffered a muscle issue in pre-season.

Add in Ibrahima Konate’s free transfer to Real Madrid and the fact Virgil van Dijk has not played since being given an extended break after the World Cup, and it is clear that the Reds desperately need extra cover at the back.

Araujo was a pillar of the Barcelona squad but only made 11 league starts last season.

The 6ft 3ins defender lost his place in the line-up after manager Hansi Flick zoned in on Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin as his preferred centre-back pairing.

Araujo also missed part of the campaign as he took a break from football to cope with anxiety and depression.

“I feel different and I’m happy about it, because I’m more at ease, happier. I can enjoy what I love to do, which is playing football, and that helps a lot.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’
Sports.content:
GI WHIZ Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’

UEFA paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of Gianni Infantino while he was its general secretary, it has been reported.

The woman received the money after their supposed relationship with the 56-year-old – while he was a top official at European football’s governing body, according to The Telegraph.



She is also alleged to have been promoted by the under-fire Fifa boss during their relationship.

Senior figures at Uefa claim the married dad-of-four ensured the woman left with the pay-off.



And after she left, the football body is understood to have paid for her to do an MBA at a business school.

In a statement on Friday night, Uefa admitted that a payment had been made and that it was aware of the allegations the woman was in a relationship with Infantino.

It said it had since “tightened” its regulations to “reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation”.

Infantino joined Uefa in 2000 and spent 16 years there before leaving to become Fifa president in February 2016.



A Fifa spokesperson said: “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue.

“Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

“No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.

“All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations.”

The alleged use of Uefa funds happened while Infantino was its general secretary, sources claimed and the woman was allegedly promoted to a management position while the relationship was taking place.



Uefa’s then president Michel Platini is said to have challenged him over the alleged affair and it was agreed she would leave with a pay-off.

As well as the pay-off it also forked out for the woman to take an MBA course at a business school which charged around £45,000 per year in fees, as part of the deal.

Sources also claimed that when the woman left, Infantino allegedly used his connections to secure a new lucrative post for the woman in a similar field.

A spokesman for Uefa said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school.

“The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.



“Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino, it is claimed, promoted his alleged lover, handing her a 30 per cent pay rise and a salary of around £147,000.

Her rapid rise is said to have raised eyebrows among colleagues and concerns he could be abusing his position to advance her.

During his time at Uefa he oversaw a footballing empire which had revenues of around £1.2billion and covered the game in 53 countries.

Infantino met his wife Leena Al Ashqar when she was working for the Lebanese Football Federation.



The pair married in 2001 and have four children.

It is not known if his wife was aware of the alleged relationship.

Matters are said to have come to a head when Platini learned about it, reports say.

A well-placed source told The Telegraph: “He made a huge mistake and it almost cost him his career.

“People [within Uefa] were telling Platini, ‘You have to fire him’.”



Another added: “Platini challenged Gianni, saying something like ‘she or you?’ and Gianni said, ‘She will leave’, and she left.”

Sources also claimed that Platini told Infantino that either he or the woman would have to leave.

The revelations come just a week after the collapse of Infantino’s financing scheme, which he announced nine days after the end of the World Cup.

The plan would have resulted in a group of investors controlling the commercial interests of Fifa’s top competitions for both men and women.

Uefa revolted against the plan, voting 55-0 to boycott the next World Cup, a move which helped defeat the plan.



It accused Fifa of attempting to trade away football’s soul.

The Concacaf nations in North and Central America then followed Uefa’s lead and condemned the plan.

Fifa is a non-profit organisation which means in theory money made from the competition is ploughed back into football.

Infantino is said to have told his inner circle he has no plans to quit, having met senior staff in Morocco this week and he has allegedly appealed to US President Donald Trump for support.

Sports.title: Sky Sports legend Chris Kamara reveals cancer scare and urges men to get tested as he prepares for Great North Run
Sports.content:
CHRIS KAMARA revealed he had a prostate cancer scare.

And now he is urging men to bury their pride and embarrassment and get tested.



The Sky Sports legend, 68, has been supporting Prostate Cancer UK’s work for a decade, including ten charity walks with pal Jeff Stelling.

But a health scare after a routine blood test in 2024 sparked alarm bells for the former Swindon and Brentford midfielder – before he was given good news that it was not cancer.



Kammy told the Mirror: “Any man would feel scared about the prospect of getting prostate cancer.

“I’ve been working with the charity for more than a decade, so I know that early diagnosis is absolutely key.

“A routine test I had two years ago flagged up a slightly PSA level raised level.

“That was a scary thing to hear, but thankfully it turned out I didn’t have prostate cancer. After consistent monitoring, my levels remain the same.

“As men, it’s so important we look after ourselves and keep an eye on any changes.

“I do get up in the night to pee more now. But that’s a symptom of other conditions too, so check with your GP.



What is prostate cancer? Prostate cancer affects a small, walnut shaped gland that sits underneath the bladder and surrounds the urethra – the tube carrying pee outside the body. It usually grows bigger as you get older. The prostate’s main job is to help make semen – the fluid that carries sperm. Most men with early prostate cancer don’t have any signs or symptoms – that’s why it’s important to know about your risk. Possible symptoms include: Difficulty starting to urinate or emptying your bladder

A weak flow when you urinate

A feeling that your bladder hasn’t emptied properly

Dribbling urine after you finish urinating

Needing to urinate more often than usual, especially at night

A sudden need to urinate – you may sometimes leak urine before you get to the toilet If you do notice changes in the way you urinate, this is more likely to be a sign of an enlarged prostate, which is very common and non-cancerous. But it’s still a good idea to get it checked out. In the UK, about one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime. Some factors may mean you’re more likely to get it. This includes: Getting older – it mainly affects men aged 50 or over

Having a family history of prostate cancer

Being Black If you have any of these risk factors or if you have any symptoms, speak to your GP. They can talk to you about your risk, and about the tests that are used to diagnose prostate cancer. Source: Prostate Cancer UK

“And I know none of us likes going to the doctor about ‘problems below the belt’ – but it’s a mountain you have to climb, so just do it.

“Doing the walks alongside my great mate Jeff and meeting so many affected by prostate cancer, or who were marching in honour of loved ones they had lost, really brought it home to me.

“Those stories are heartbreaking and inspirational at the same time, and having that knowledge of the disease certainly helped me deal with my scare.

“I want to raise as much awareness as I can, particularly for black men, who are at double the risk.



“Prostate Cancer UK have a brilliant risk checker on their website. It takes 30 seconds and may just save your life.

“The problem with prostate checking, it’s your genitals, and you feel embarrassed when you shouldn’t be.

“These doctors and nurses have seen it all before. Get over that problem and go and get yourself checked.”

Rather than climbing a mountain, as he did with Kilimanjaro in 2012, Kamara is preparing to run a half-marathon.

He is set to take on the 13.1-mile challenge at next month’s Great North Run in Newcastle to raise more money for Prostate Cancer UK.



Fittingly, Kammy is doing it alongside son Jack and fellow broadcaster Ben Shephard, who have both supported him through his other major health battle.

Kamara was diagnosed with speech apraxia due to an underactive thyroid – causing him to lose his ability to speak as usual and feeling like a “fraud”.

After various treatments and forms of recovery, Kamara has got the confidence to be back on TV – in large part thanks to Shephard, to whom Kamara went public with his condition in a Good Morning Britain interview in 2023.

Kamara – who is hoping to finish in three hours – added: “Ben has been amazing. He’s part of the reason I came back to do TV.

“He convinced me to do that GMB interview with him. I’m back partly down to his help and encouragement.



“I spent a couple of years feeling sorry for myself and thinking, ‘This is totally beyond me to ever consider getting back to walking, never mind jogging.’

“I wanted to give myself a real challenge to try and get back to somewhere near the person I was.

“I’m helping a lot of charities these days. I thought, ‘What would be the perfect challenge for me?’ To do a half marathon and make it to the finish line with all my problems.

“Going down stairs I’m not so good, so going down hills is going to be a massive challenge.

“But Ben and my son Jack will guide me through that. They will make sure I get it done.”

Sports.title: Declan Rice leads kind wishes after Arsenal starlet’s heartbreaking post as he confirms ruptured ACL in Real Betis loss
Sports.content:
ARSENAL starlet Louie Copley took to social media to confirm that he has ruptured his ACL.

And Declan Rice was among a slew of Gunners stars to leave a supportive comment under Copley’s Instagram post.



Arsenal academy graduate Copley, 19, replaced Ben White as a half-time substitute as his side took on Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday.

He was forced off just nine minutes later, however, after horribly twisting his knee – leaving fans fearing the worst.



After the game, boss Mikel Arteta gave a gloomy update, saying: “Well, probably we’re going to have it tomorrow. It doesn’t look good, the mechanism is not too positive, the symptoms that he already has either.

“So let’s hope that tomorrow the news is better.”



Later confirming his unfortunate news, Copley wrote on Instagram, alongside a snap of himself in agony: “Words can’t describe how I’m feeling right now, to making my pre season debut for the team I’ve grown up supporting to finding out I’ve ruptured my ACL.

“The road ahead won’t be easy but I’ll give everything to come back stronger and better”.

Rice commented with a heart emoji, as did fellow Arsenal stars White, Max Dowman and Myles Lewis-Skelly – in addition to other academy players too.

Jurrien Timber left a praying emoji, while Charles Sagoe Jr, currently on loan at Swedish side Kalmar, added: “Speedy recovery Lou, get well soon!!!”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Full-back Copley has established himself as one of the Arsenal academy’s brightest talents in recent years.

The Essex-born starlet joined Crawley Town on loan in January, playing nine times during the second half of last term in his first taste of senior men’s football.

With Copley forced off, lacklustre Arsenal went on to lose 3-1 to Real Betis.

The Gunners will be back in action on Sunday as they host Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd ace Nicky Butt has rubbish tip ban lifted — thanks to The Sun
Sports.content:
EX-Manchester United ace Nicky Butt has had his rubbish tip ban lifted — thanks to The Sun.

We told how the “raging” former midfielder, 51, rowed with staff after being told his Range Rover was deemed a commercial vehicle as the seats were down.



But bosses contacted us to say they do not have a policy stating that car seat positions change a vehicle’s classification.

They say residents are asked at the gate what they have brought so staff can direct them to the right container.



Butt was believed to have visited the Woodhouse Lane Recycling Centre in Altrincham.

Recycle for Greater Manchester said: “We’re sorry to hear about Nicky’s experience.



“But would like to reassure him that he’s still very welcome to use any of the 19 recycling centres.”

Former England ace Butt told The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast that he dumped his “smelly bags” at the centre near his home in Cheshire despite being chased by an attendant with a walkie-talkie.

The Class of 92 hero said: “I thought, well, I’m there now, I’m gonna go for it.

“So I’ve got up the ramp, I see this bloke getting up…trying to chase me up the hill, but he’s got his walkie-talkie out.



“So I’ve literally got up the top, throw all the bags out, and I’m going back down the hill, and he’s going mad at me.

“Anyway, I’m banned from the tip.”

Sports.title: Arsenal ready to hijack Liverpool’s £130million Bradley Barcola transfer from PSG after missing out on Vinicius Jr
Sports.content:
ARSENAL could look to hijack Liverpool’s swoop for Bradley Barcola after missing out on Vinicius Jr.

The Gunners had been plotting a blockbuster move for the Real Madrid winger, only for him to pen a new six-year deal at the Bernabeu.



Arsenal chiefs were committed to completing a big-money transfer for the Brazilian, who had one year remaining on his previous contract.

But Vinicius Jr instead opted to sign a new £480,000-a-week extension to stay put, ruling the Gunners out of the race.



Mikel Arteta‘s side remain desperate to land a new left winger, particularly after letting Leandro Trossard join Besiktas.

According to the Independent, Barcola is an “attractive option” for the Gunners.

But they will have to play “catch up” to Liverpool, who have already been negotiating personal terms.

The Reds are eager to land the Paris Saint-Germain winger as they seek a new star winger following Mo Salah’s departure.

Andoni Iraola‘s side have identified Barcola as a key target and have been working on the transfer for weeks.

But PSG’s asking price remains a stumbling block for all interested suitors, with Luis Enrique‘s men said to be demanding around £130million.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

And, according to French outlet Canal Plus, the Reds have told PSG they do not have the means to match their sky-high asking price.

That could now leave the door open for the Gunners to swoop.

Barcola, 23, has played 152 times for the French giants since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals and contributing towards two Champions Leagues and three Ligue 1 titles.

The winger came on as an 83rd minute substitute as PSG beat Arsenal in last season’s Champions League final back in May.



Given PSG’s summer business, he may be about to fall down the pecking order at Parc des Princes.

Following permanent exits for Lee Kang-in, Goncalo Ramos and Randal Kolo Muani, PSG signed French international attacker Maghnes Akliouche on Friday.

They are also keen on Ajax attacker Mika Godts, with Barcelona‘s World Cup final hero Ferran Torres also linked.



In addition to Barcola, Arsenal admire Atletico Madrid star Julian Alvarez.

A deal will be very difficult to accomplish, however, with the former Manchester City forward more likely to stay in LaLiga.

Another option is Everton ace Iliman Ndiaye.

The impressive Toffees star’s future on Merseyside looks uncertain, with Saudi side Al-Hilal also in the mix.

Arsenal gave a lacklustre display as they were beaten 3-1 by Real Betis in Dublin earlier this week.

Quizzed about the mood in the dressing room after the match, Arteta pulled no punches.

The Spaniard said: “They are very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Sports.title: Arsenal should sign Man Utd star Marcus Rashford after both sides had transfer dreams scuppered by El Clasico giants
Sports.content:
BOTH Marcus Rashford and Arsenal have seen their transfer dreams scuppered by the Clasico giants this summer.

Rashford, 28, was first to suffer when Barcelona snubbed the chance to land him in a £26million permanent deal after last season’s loan at the Nou Camp.



Instead the Catalans decided to splash out £69m on his England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Arsenal’s own blow arrived on Thursday evening when top transfer target Vinicius Jr ended his flirtation with them by signing a new deal at Real Madrid worth a staggering £480,000 a week.



So, with both the Gunners and Rashford left licking their wounds, is it time they came together to solve each others’ problems?

Rashford is set to reunite with his Manchester United team-mates on Sunday for the first time in 18 months.

The forward is due to travel to Dublin for United’s pre-season training camp after completing his mandatory three-week post-World Cup break.

Rashford has not trained with United since January 2025 after loan spells with Aston Villa and then Barca.

Rashford and Alejandro Garnacho – now on loan at Villa from Chelsea – were part of a five-man ‘bomb squad’ isolated at United’s training ground last summer.

They were ordered by then-boss Ruben Amorim to report for separate training times to the main squad.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Although Amorim was sacked in January and head coach Michael Carrick has stabilised United, the imminent reunion is still awkward for all parties.

Rashford publicly declared his wish to join Barcelona permanently in May and doubled down on his desire to leave permanently during the World Cup.

But the England international’s £325,000-a-week salary – signed before Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Old Trafford involvement – has effectively blocked a permanent departure.

On the eve of the World Cup, Rashford posted a brief message on his Instagram page thanking Barcelona, Villa, England and their respective coaches.



There was no mention of United, the club he has been at since the age of seven.

United are also conspicuous by their absence on the bios of Rashford’s social media accounts.

Senior United figures were surprised by Barcelona’s decision not to buy Rashford, which has left them out of options.

United sources have repeatedly stressed they will not let Rashford leave on another season-long loan.

The academy graduate is under contract until 2028.



Rashford’s first appearance back at United could be in their final pre-season friendly against AC Milan, who are now managed by Amorim.

Arsenal wanted Brazilian ace Vinicius as their marquee signing to launch their first Prem title defence in 22 years.

They were led down the garden path and ended it with the sight of the Brazilian scrawling his signature on a new six-year Real contract.

But there are alternative left wingers on the market and Rashford is one of them.

Arsenal have been here before, with Raheem Sterling two years ago.



What appeared a canny deal turned out to be anything but.

Sterling’s slide has been so steep he is currently without a club and was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving in May.

Rashford is a downgrade on Vinicius – well, who isn’t? – but he ticks a lot of boxes for Arsenal: Premier League pedigree, Champions League clout, big-club nous, winners’ medals, international experience and with a point to prove.

Rashford has incentives aplenty to show he is too young for the riches of Turkey or Saudi Arabia.



He has hopes of representing England again at the Euros in 2028 as well as the 2030 World Cup.

When Rashford first steeled himself to leave United, he was insistent on playing for a Champions League club.

That would rule out Tottenham – but don’t bet against them making their own move, with boss Roberto Di Zerbi promising a “bomba” signing.

Spurs nor Rashford’s entourage have dampened speculation.

Tottenham have spent more than £200m on signings already, blowing United out of the water to buy Mateus Fernandes.



If they wanted to, Tottenham could foot the bill for Rashford’s £325,000 weekly salary.

Spurs are also lacking dynamism in attack, with James Maddison, who missed most of last season with an ACL injury and then sustained a minor problem in pre-season and Dejan Kulusevski on his way back from a patella injury he suffered in May 2025.

It suits Rashford to be linked with two of the Premier League’s biggest clubs after Barcelona deemed Gordon a better investment.

Well-placed sources have said a move to Arsenal for Rashford, however fanciful, is not a total non-starter.



Rashford has kept a low profile during his summer break but preparations have been made for his return to Manchester.

The circumstances aren’t ideal but he at least has a club.

Jadon Sancho, another winger now off the books at United, put non-league minnows Flixton on the map by using their training facilities.

Sancho is a free agent, at least.

For Rashford, he is running out of time in a transfer window that closes in less than four weeks.



Even with his steep salary, Rashford is more appealing than Sancho.

He started matches for England at the World Cup, scored in the 4-2 group stage win against Croatia and contributed to a Barcelona title triumph last season.

When push comes to shove, something can happen out of nothing in the final days of a transfer window.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Rashford’s temporary move to Villa materialised with less than 72 hours until it closed.

For now, there will be much to ponder for him and Arsenal as the new season rapidly approaches.

Sports.title: 'I'd rather fight Aaron for world title' - Walsh dismisses Stevie McKenna call-out
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh would entertain a fight against Aaron McKenna over Stephen McKenna, insisting all-Irish clashes only make sense with the world title on the line.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) fights former European champion Tyler Denny on the undercard of Aaron McKenna's IBF world middleweight title showdown with Etinosa Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

It's the headline act of six middleweight bouts on a stacked card that also sees Stephen McKenna face Owen O'Neill over eight rounds before assuming corner duties for his younger, world title-chasing brother.

Walsh has been identified as a potential future opponent by Stephen McKenna (16-1, 15 KOs), but the unbeaten 25-year-old believes he's already at another level.

Responding to McKenna's challenge, Walsh told Sky Sports: "If there's anyone that I'm looking at, it would be the fella with the world title, not the fella with the loss.

"In my mind, it doesn't make sense unless it's for a world title. There are bigger names than Stevie McKenna calling me out.

"Shane Mosley Jr is a bigger fight than Stevie McKenna. His brother Aaron is fighting for the world title. If I was going to fight either of them, I'd fight Aaron for the world title."

Image: Walsh on the scales ahead of his middleweight fight against Denny (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa Boxing)

'It makes sense for him, not for me'

Walsh believes an all-Irish fight without a world title on the line could needlessly jeopardise the momentum middleweights are currently generating in Ireland.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," he added. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing. Why would we want to eliminate each other unless it's for a world title?

"If it's for a world title, at least you can get paid for it. You're going to be able to sell out an arena and put on a big show for everyone involved. Why have an all-Irish fight on an undercard somewhere when it doesn't make sense?

"It makes sense for him. It makes no sense at all for me. His brother's fighting for the world title. There are bigger names calling me out. I've had bigger fights. It doesn't make any sense."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stevie McKenna is determined to have an all-Ireland clash against Walsh should both of them emerge victorious at Zuffa Boxing 10 this weekend

Walsh believes Stephen McKenna would be better served avenging his sole loss as a professional, a majority-decision defeat to Lee Cutler in 2024.

"He doesn't even want to fight the fella who beat him," he said. "He was asked if he wanted a rematch and he said no.

"Go back and fight the fella who beat you. That's the one I'd be looking at if I was him. He's in the same division, the same league, and he's begging for the rematch."

'I'll fight Aaron or the other fella'

Walsh, who fights in Dublin for the first time since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024, is confident he can overcome Denny and believes Aaron McKenna will become Ireland's newest world champion.

Victory for both men would set up the mouth-watering prospect of an all-Irish world title fight, and Walsh insists he would have no problem facing Aaron should he emerge as champion.

"I don't know much about his opponent, to be honest," Walsh added. "I'm sure Aaron will win. I presume he will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Walsh insists he's not complacent ahead of Saturday's fight with Denny, while the former European champion is confident he can cause the upset in Dublin

"It's a big opportunity and a big night for him to go out there, perform and win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

"If Aaron wins and they want me to fight him, I'll fight him. If he doesn't win, maybe I'll fight the other fella.

"I just fight whoever they tell me to. I'm not out here calling anybody out. It's just the same old habits."

Sports.title: Bracey shares memories of Lawrence ahead of Sunday's tribute
Sports.content:
When James Bracey thinks of Syd Lawrence, he does not first think of wickets, records or milestones.

He thinks of a man who never stopped giving to Gloucestershire cricket.

This Sunday, Gloucestershire will honour former England fast bowler Syd Lawrence during their Metro Bank One Day Cup fixture against Nottinghamshire, wearing a special commemorative kit and raising funds for the Motor Neurone Disease Association (MNDA).

For Bracey, the occasion is deeply personal.

One memory stands above all others: September 2024, when Gloucestershire won the T20 Blast for the first time in the club's history. Lawrence, already battling motor neurone disease, was there to present the trophy.

"That was very special for me," Bracey tells Sky Sports.

Image: For Bracey, his standout memory of Lawrence comes from that exchange - Photo courtesy of Gloucestershire CCC

"We were obviously delighted that we'd just won the Blast for the first time as a team, but to see how much it meant to him, even at that stage of his life, was really emotional.

"It just showed how much he really loved the club. To see his face when he was able to hold that trophy was really special for me."

Image: Photo courtesy of Gloucestershire CCC

Lawrence, who passed away in June 2025 aged 61, remains one of the most influential figures in Gloucestershire's history. He became the first British-born Black cricketer to play Test cricket for England in 1988 and later became Gloucestershire's first Black president.

Although Bracey never saw Lawrence play, his impact on the club was impossible to miss.

"From my experiences, he was an incredibly kind-hearted person, incredibly personable and cared a hell of a lot about Gloucestershire cricket," Bracey said.

"Any time he was around the ground, he was chatting to everyone. He was larger than life and had a hell of a lot of energy."

Sunday's tribute is also designed to raise awareness of motor neurone disease and highlight the work of the MNDA.

"We've seen how public Syd was with his condition," Bracey said. "But the impact it has on family and friends is just as important.

"That's the amazing thing about what the MNDA do. They support the person with the disease, but they also help those around them."

Image: A pioneering Black cricketer, Lawrence helped open doors for future generations

Lawrence's legacy also extends beyond Gloucestershire. As a pioneering Black cricketer, he helped open doors for future generations.

"There's been a lot of progress," Bracey said. "But there's obviously a lot more work to do in maintaining that progress and increasing it as well."

As Gloucestershire and Nottinghamshire come together to honour Lawrence, Bracey hopes supporters remember the cricketer, the trailblazer and the person behind both.

"When I'm reminded of Syd, it takes me back to that day," he said.

"It was a very special and happy moment for me to see what that meant to him."

This weekend's tribute will celebrate a man whose love for Gloucestershire never faded - and whose legacy continues to inspire the club he loved.

Sports.title: Araujo set for surprise Liverpool loan move
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to join on loan for the season.

The deal is a straight loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract until 2031 last year.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

The 27-year-old centre-back will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over relatively inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

The summer signing from Rennes has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Sports.title: McKenna vs Oliha and Walsh vs Denny big-fight predictions
Sports.content:
Experts have their say ahead of the Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha middleweight world championship clash and Callum Walsh's crucial fight against Tyler Denny, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.

Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha

Chris Billam-Smith (former cruiserweight champion): McKenna's got so much to his game I think. He's shown he can box a bit but he's got an intensity and a workrate. He punches hard enough to get people's respect. We saw a lot from him in the Liam Smith fight, of what he can do. I will pick him to win, probably on points, but he could overwhelm him as well.

Johnny Nelson (former cruiserweight champion): Aaron McKenna gets an inside-the-distance stoppage win I think. His engine, his pace will be too much.

Oliha can't afford to get hit too easily because McKenna won't leave you alone. It's a good fight, especially for McKenna boxing in Dublin for the first time in his professional career.

I think McKenna in the first half of the fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McKenna and Oliha were locked in a tense face-off ahead of their IBF world middleweight title clash

Johnny Fisher (heavyweight star): McKenna's been based in America for a little while, this is now his homecoming fight. Tremendous amateur record, hopefully that pedigree comes through. I think this crowd will give him that extra lift. If he uses that crowd and doesn't let it be detrimental to him, that's what's going to carry him over the line.

Callum Walsh (middleweight contender): I presume that Aaron will win. It's a big night, a big opportunity for him to go out there and perform and to win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

Connor Coyle (middleweight contender): I think McKenna will win, I think he'll win on points. I know McKenna's boxing, I've known him growing up through Irish boxing. That's why I know he's a good boxer.

I think he'll become IBF world champion on Saturday night.

Sports.title: Debut Lankshear goal sees Boro past Wrexham as Wolves & Stevenage progress
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear's debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round.

Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener, but while Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter's cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle's cross, and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt.

Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento's cross into Lankshear's path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining, but Morgan Whittaker's low strike rebounded off the post.

Wolves coast past Port Vale as Jimenez makes return

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Wolves' clash with Port Vale in the first round of the Carabao Cup.

Wolves progressed with a comfortable 3-0 win over Port Vale in which all three goals came in the first half. Adam Armstrong, Andre and Fer Lopez took the game away from the League Two side as Cesar Peixoto marked his first game in charge with a win.

Jon Brady's Port Vale had opportunities. Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel hooked an extraordinary chance away from the Wolves goal before the break, before Mo Faal's low penalty was saved by the legs of Dan Bentley to deny the travelling fans a consolation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Port Vale's Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel misses a chance from six yards out in his side's Carabao Cup clash with Wolves.

The Wolves supporters among the crowd of 21,360 at Molineux were more interested in serenading their returning hero. Raul Jimenez, the club's Premier League top scorer, re-signed this summer after three years at Fulham and came on as a late substitute.

The Mexican centre-forward did fire off one fierce shot on goal but he was unable to mark the occasion with a goal that would have been cruel on a competitive Port Vale side. But it is Wolves who take their place in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Stevenage strike late to beat Wycombe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round Carabao Cup match between Wycombe Wanderers and Stevenage.

New signing Josh Magennis headed the winner in the dying seconds to send Stevenage through to the second round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-1 victory at Wycombe.

It was a fitting start to the Boro's 50th anniversary season as substitute Magennis, a summer capture from Exeter, rose to score from Phoenix Patterson's left-wing corner in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

The visitors had shaken off early pressure to take the lead against the run of play in the 27th minute.

Midfielder Dan Kemp took advantage of hesitancy in the Wycombe defence as he raced through to fire home a low shot.

That stung the home side into action and Ewan Henderson equalised in the 38th minute. Winger Silko Thomas crossed from the left and the Scot slipped through the visiting defence to score right-footed from just outside the six-yard box.

Stevenage scared their Sky Bet League One rivals again on the stroke of half-time when Kemp rattled the bar with a shot from the edge of the box.

Wycombe took control after the break but struggled to break through.

New boy Emre Tezgel, on for Cauley Woodrow, was thwarted by Boro skipper Carl Piergianni as he attempted to force home Thomas' cross from the left in the 77th minute before Magennis settled the issue.

The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every first-round tie available to watch live on Sky Sports!

West Ham, Burnley and Leicester are among those in action on Saturday - and you can follow the goals as they go in from all 29 ties on Soccer Saturday.

Every match from the opening round will be shown live on Sky Sports, with clubs from the Championship, League One and League Two entering the competition.

Sports.title: New Zealand begin South Africa tour with flattering win over Stormers
Sports.content:
New Zealand's first full-scale tour of South Africa in 30 years began with an underwhelming 38-21 win over the Stormers.

The scoreline flattered a scratch All Blacks side which was favoured to win comfortably.

The makeshift Stormers - in pre-season mode - rallied twice to tie the score, which was knotted at 14-14 until 13 minutes to go.

When the Stormers lost their second scrum-half and had no more reserve backs, the patched-up backline was ruthlessly exposed by New Zealand, who scored three tries in the last eight minutes.

Image: New Zealand started with an unconvincing win on their tour of South Africa

The good news for the All Blacks was they appeared to finish with no major injuries, seven players made their first appearance in the black jersey this year, and two more made their debuts off the bench; prop Siale Lauaki and inside back Josh Jacomb.

But the most impressive players in the stadium were Stormers fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed, who looked comfortably cool in his first-class debut at age 20, and flanker Deon Fourie, the dynamo who will be 40 next month.

"It was a good introduction for us to South African rugby," said New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie. "We started ​very well and it looked like which side had the ball ⁠got rewarded by the referee.

"When we had ⁠the ball we were really dangerous. We knew they would bring line speed [in defence]. We just weren't quite clinical enough ‌to expose them.

"They came at us with their set-piece and we need to be better in those areas. We expected a lot of aerial attacks and we probably did ‌not handle that as well as we could have."

A swipe at fake news

Monday 27 July

Gianni Infantino marks the end of the World Cup by taking to Instagram with a 15-page post calling out the media for trying to sully it. He says it was a month of “joy and happiness”, and “those sitting behind their pens and papers, behind their screens, spreading hate and false rumours” about greed and his relationship with Donald Trump had let themselves down – “while we at Fifa are on the frontlines, working hard”. He says journalists should step back and instead “take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray or watch a match”.

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.
